It must not be described, in this manifest or any downstream artifact, as a historically best-performing target, an empirically selected optimum, or the output of any search. It was one of five preregistered, no-search grid points; the specific choice to freeze 1.5R rather than 0.5R (or 1.0R/2.0R) has no committed historical rationale document anywhere in the repository -- see historical_provenance_limitation.

historical_provenance_limitation.statement: candidate_spec.yaml's own header comments cite this exact file (candidate_manifest.json) and 'the preregistered P4 structural-compromise rationale' as the historical justification for freezing 1.5R specifically. Neither exists anywhere in the repository, on main or on refactor/architecture-boundary-hardening-v3 (confirmed by the HYP_001_LINEAGE_AUDIT, phase1 and phase6). This manifest does not fabricate that missing rationale. The true historical record is: 1.5R was one of five preregistered grid points evaluated with no search (P6, commit 9852c52, refactor branch), was declared as the frozen v1.1.0 value in candidate_spec.yaml (commit 53b7215, main) without any committed document explaining the specific choice, and no further explanation has since been located or reconstructed.

owner_prospective_freeze_decision.reason: 1.5R is the already-declared HYP_001 candidate value; preserving it for the fresh confirmatory test avoids selecting a NEW target after observing additional GEN_002 exit/MFE evidence, which would itself be a form of post-hoc, evidence-informed parameter selection. This is a PROSPECTIVE governance decision about what to test going forward -- it does not retroactively establish that 1.5R was historically well-justified.
owner_prospective_freeze_decision.explicit_confirmation: No new target value (0.5R, 1.0R, 2.0R, or any other) was tested, computed, or compared during this governance mission. This mission performed zero economic evaluation.
